questions.question: Do two visually distinct surface types each occupy at least a quarter of the patch?
questions.definition: Count differences in color and texture that indicate different surfaces, excluding differences caused solely by shadow.

questions.question: Does one continuous, visually uniform area occupy between one-third and two-thirds of the patch?
questions.definition: Treat an area as uniform when its dominant color and texture remain similar despite small internal features.

questions.question: Is the patch divided into two contrasting parts by a prominent boundary?
questions.definition: Count a boundary extending at least halfway across the patch with visibly different surface patterns on its two sides.

questions.question: Do at least three substantial areas meet near the center of the patch?
questions.definition: Count distinct areas each covering at least 5% of the patch whose boundaries meet within the central third.

questions.question: Are straight boundaries more prominent than curved boundaries?
questions.definition: Compare the combined visible lengths of major surface boundaries, ignoring the image frame and very small features.

questions.question: Do curved or irregular boundaries separate at least three substantial areas?
questions.definition: Count areas covering at least 5% of the patch whose shared boundaries visibly bend or meander.

questions.question: Is one surface type visibly fragmented into at least five separate pieces?
questions.definition: Count pieces with matching color and texture separated by clearly different surfaces, excluding isolated single-pixel variations.

questions.question: Is a contrasting area completely enclosed by another surface type?
questions.definition: Count an enclosed area covering at least 2% of the patch with no visible connection to the image edge.

questions.question: Does a narrow linear feature connect opposite sides of the patch?
questions.definition: Count a visible road, water feature, vegetation strip, or comparable corridor narrower than one-tenth of the patch width.

questions.question: Does a broad band of one surface type cross the patch?
questions.definition: Count a connected band between one-tenth and one-third of the patch width that reaches two opposite image edges.

questions.question: Are most major boundaries aligned in one common direction?
questions.definition: Count a shared alignment when more than half the visible length of major boundaries falls within approximately 20 degrees of one orientation.

questions.question: Are two different boundary orientations prominent in separate parts of the patch?
questions.definition: Count two groups of at least three boundaries whose dominant directions differ by approximately 30 degrees or more.

questions.question: Is the pattern noticeably finer on one side of the patch than on the other?
questions.definition: Count a contrast where typical visible surface units on one side are approximately half the width of those on the other.

questions.question: Does a large uniform area adjoin a mosaic of smaller areas?
questions.definition: Count a uniform area covering at least a quarter of the patch that shares a boundary with at least four smaller contrasting units.

questions.question: Are at least three elongated surface units arranged side by side?
questions.definition: Count units at least three times longer than wide that share a broadly similar orientation.

questions.question: Does a branching network structure the visible landscape?
questions.definition: Count connected linear features with at least three visible junctions that separate or connect substantial surface areas.

questions.question: Is there a gradual transition between contrasting surfaces?
questions.definition: Count a transition at least approximately 50 meters wide in which color or texture changes progressively rather than at a sharp boundary.

questions.question: Does a narrow contrasting strip separate two large areas?
questions.definition: Count a strip under approximately 50 meters wide extending at least 300 meters between areas each covering at least 10% of the patch.

questions.question: Does the central part of the patch differ markedly from most of its perimeter?
questions.definition: Compare the dominant surface in the central third with the surface along more than half the image perimeter.

questions.question: Are three visibly different surface types arranged in successive bands?
questions.definition: Count three adjoining bands with distinct color or texture, each extending at least a quarter of the patch width.

questions.question: Does visibly vegetated ground occupy between one-quarter and three-quarters of the patch?
questions.definition: Estimate vegetation extent jointly from true-color appearance and the red vegetation response in false color.

questions.question: Is vegetation concentrated mainly in one half of the patch?
questions.definition: Count a concentration when one horizontal or vertical half contains roughly twice as much visibly vegetated area as the other.

questions.question: Does the vegetation form at least three disconnected substantial patches?
questions.definition: Count vegetated patches each covering at least 2% of the image and separated by visibly nonvegetated surfaces.

questions.question: Does a continuous vegetation corridor link two larger vegetated areas?
questions.definition: Count a visible vegetated connection narrower than both areas it joins, with no clearly resolved nonvegetated break.

questions.question: Are narrow vegetation strips a prominent part of the patch?
questions.definition: Count at least three vegetation strips each approximately 100 meters long and no more than 50 meters wide.

questions.question: Are both smooth and coarse vegetation textures present over substantial areas?
questions.definition: Count each texture when it occupies at least 5% of the patch, with coarse texture showing repeated resolved tonal irregularities.

questions.question: Does a coarse-textured vegetation block have a straight edge?
questions.definition: Count a woody-looking vegetation block with a boundary remaining approximately straight for at least 200 meters.

questions.question: Does a coarse-textured vegetation block have a deeply indented edge?
questions.definition: Count an edge with at least two visible indentations extending approximately 50 meters or more into the block.

questions.question: Are open gaps visible inside a larger vegetation block?
questions.definition: Count at least two clearly resolved gaps with weaker vegetation signals that are surrounded by the same connected vegetation block.

questions.question: Does vegetation along a boundary appear denser than vegetation in the adjoining interior?
questions.definition: Count a continuous margin at least 100 meters long with a stronger red vegetation response and less exposed substrate than the adjacent interior.

questions.question: Do neighboring vegetated areas have markedly different false-color tones?
questions.definition: Count adjoining areas each covering at least 2% of the patch whose dominant vegetation tones differ clearly beyond small local fluctuations.

questions.question: Does one continuous vegetated area contain a broad gradient in vegetation signal?
questions.definition: Count a progressive change in false-color red intensity extending approximately 100 meters or more without a clear intervening boundary.

questions.question: Does a vegetated area contain irregular patches with a weaker vegetation signal?
questions.definition: Count at least three resolved internal patches that are less red in false color than their surroundings and do not match obvious shadows.

questions.question: Are stronger vegetation signals arranged in bands within a larger area?
questions.definition: Count at least three resolved bands that are redder in false color than the intervening surface.

questions.question: Are green-looking and yellow-brown-looking vegetated areas both substantial?
questions.definition: Count each appearance over at least 5% of the patch where texture or false color supports a vegetation interpretation.

questions.question: Does yellow-brown vegetation form a continuous area rather than only scattered spots?
questions.definition: Count a connected yellow-brown vegetated area covering at least 10% of the patch, excluding clearly bare soil.

questions.question: Do some pale or brown-looking areas retain a visible vegetation response in false color?
questions.definition: Count an area covering at least 2% of the patch that looks pale or brown in true color but has a spatially matching red vegetation signal.

questions.question: Does sparse vegetation visibly intermingle with exposed ground?
questions.definition: Count an area covering at least 5% of the patch with a resolved mixture of vegetation signals and bare-looking substrate.

questions.question: Are dense-looking and sparse-looking vegetation directly adjacent?
questions.definition: Count a shared boundary at least 100 meters long between nearly continuous vegetation and vegetation visibly mixed with exposed ground.

questions.question: Does a vegetation boundary become much clearer in false color than in true color?
questions.definition: Count a boundary at least 200 meters long whose vegetation contrast is conspicuous in false color but weak in true color.

questions.question: Does vegetation form a branching pattern through more open ground?
questions.definition: Count connected vegetation strips with at least two branch points and a total visible extent of approximately 300 meters or more.

questions.question: Are several isolated coarse-textured vegetation clumps scattered through smoother ground?
questions.definition: Count at least three resolved woody-looking clumps separated from one another by smoother vegetation or exposed ground.

questions.question: Does a woody-looking vegetation block contain two broad tonal zones?
questions.definition: Count adjoining zones each approximately 100 meters across with consistently different false-color vegetation tones, excluding obvious illumination effects.

questions.question: Is the interior of a vegetation block more uniform than its margins?
questions.definition: Count a block covering at least 10% of the patch whose margins show clearly greater color or texture variation than its central area.

questions.question: Does a narrow vegetation strip stand out against pale or brown surroundings?
questions.definition: Count a strip at least 200 meters long with a clear red vegetation signal bordered predominantly by pale or brown surfaces.

questions.question: Are contrasting vegetation conditions distributed as a fine mosaic?
questions.definition: Count at least five adjoining vegetation units under approximately 150 meters across that alternate between clearly different color or signal states.

questions.question: Do large vegetation areas look internally uniform despite differing from one another?
questions.definition: Count at least two areas each covering 10% of the patch that have relatively uniform interiors but clearly different dominant vegetation tones.

questions.question: Does vegetation extend into an otherwise nonvegetated area as a tongue or wedge?
questions.definition: Count a vegetated projection at least approximately 100 meters long that is bordered on both sides by nonvegetated ground.

questions.question: Are vegetation patches connected only by narrow visible necks?
questions.definition: Count at least one connection less than one-third the width of the two substantial vegetated areas it joins.

questions.question: Is a sharp change in vegetation appearance aligned with a straight boundary?
questions.definition: Count a tonal or density change following an approximately straight line for at least 200 meters, excluding a shadow edge.

questions.question: Are at least three field-like parcels visibly distinguishable?
questions.definition: Count bounded, relatively smooth areas whose geometric arrangement supports a field interpretation, even if their crop types cannot be identified.

questions.question: Do field-like parcels occupy between one-quarter and three-quarters of the patch?
questions.definition: Estimate the combined area of visibly bounded agricultural-looking parcels, including vegetated and bare-looking interiors.

questions.question: Are both large and small field-like parcels present?
questions.definition: Count at least two examples in each size group where the larger visible parcels have approximately four times the area of the smaller ones.

questions.question: Are at least three field-like parcels long and narrow?
questions.definition: Count visibly bounded parcels with lengths at least three times their widths, using only the portion visible when a boundary meets the image edge.

questions.question: Do several field-like parcels share a rectangular arrangement?
questions.definition: Count at least three parcels with mostly straight sides and approximately right-angle corners.

questions.question: Do several field-like parcels have irregular outlines?
questions.definition: Count at least three parcels with substantial curved sides, oblique corners, or indentations rather than approximately rectangular outlines.

questions.question: Do neighboring field-like parcels alternate between vegetated and bare-looking surfaces?
questions.definition: Count a sequence of at least three adjoining parcels in which a bare-looking parcel lies between vegetated parcels or the reverse.

questions.question: Are at least three distinct surface conditions visible among field-like parcels?
questions.definition: Count clearly different parcel appearances such as strong vegetation, weak or yellow-brown vegetation, and exposed soil without assigning crop identities.

questions.question: Is one field-like parcel visibly different from all its immediate neighbors?
questions.definition: Count a parcel sharing boundaries with at least two others whose dominant color or vegetation signal contrasts with every visible neighbor.

questions.question: Do adjacent field-like parcels have similar vegetation signals but different textures?
questions.definition: Count an adjoining pair with broadly matching false-color vegetation tones and a clear difference in smoothness, striping, or mottling.

questions.question: Are resolved parallel stripes visible within an open managed-looking area?
questions.definition: Count at least three repeated stripes within a field-like or regularly maintained area, excluding display artifacts and unresolved crop rows.

questions.question: Does one field-like parcel contain two sharply separated surface conditions?
questions.definition: Count a parcel with a recognizable common outer boundary and an internal division separating contrasting surfaces that each occupy at least one-fifth of it.

questions.question: Does a field-like parcel contain an irregular area of weaker vegetation?
questions.definition: Count a resolved weak-signal area occupying approximately 10% or more of a vegetated parcel and not following its full outer boundary.

questions.question: Do vegetation strips separate several field-like parcels?
questions.definition: Count clearly vegetated strips along at least three parcel boundaries rather than color changes between adjoining parcel interiors.

questions.question: Do several field-like parcels meet without visible woody boundaries?
questions.definition: Count at least three adjoining parcels separated by direct surface transitions or narrow bare lines with no resolved coarse-textured vegetation strip.

questions.question: Does a field-like parcel have a broad margin that differs from its interior?
questions.definition: Count a margin at least approximately 20 meters wide following two sides of a parcel and differing consistently in color or vegetation signal.

questions.question: Are bare-looking field surfaces visibly different in color from one another?
questions.definition: Count at least two agricultural-looking parcels with little vegetation response and clearly different dominant soil-like tones.

questions.question: Does a bare-looking field contain broad dark and light patches?
questions.definition: Count resolved tonal patches each approximately 50 meters across within one parcel, excluding recognizable shadows and vegetation patches.

questions.question: Do several neighboring fields have similarly strong vegetation signals?
questions.definition: Count at least three visibly separate parcels whose interiors are predominantly strong red in false color with little exposed substrate.

questions.question: Are green-looking fields interspersed with yellow-brown fields?
questions.definition: Count at least two parcels of each appearance within the same visible field mosaic, without inferring a particular season or management event.

questions.question: Does a field-like parcel wrap around a contrasting feature?
questions.definition: Count a parcel that borders at least three sides of a woody patch, built feature, water feature, or other clearly different surface.

questions.question: Does a woody-looking patch interrupt an otherwise regular field pattern?
questions.definition: Count a coarse-textured vegetation patch that forces at least two neighboring field boundaries to bend or terminate.

questions.question: Do narrow access-like lines divide or connect several fields?
questions.definition: Count visible nonvegetated linear routes that border or enter at least three field-like parcels and appear connected.

questions.question: Is a small built-looking cluster embedded in a field mosaic?
questions.definition: Count a resolved cluster of roof-like angular surfaces and associated hard ground bordered on at least three sides by field-like parcels.

questions.question: Do field boundaries change direction around a curved feature?
questions.definition: Count at least three field edges that visibly adjust their orientation alongside a curving road, vegetation belt, or water feature.

questions.question: Are repeated vegetation bands visible across more than one managed parcel?
questions.definition: Count at least two parcels containing resolved, regularly spaced vegetation bands without requiring identification as orchards, vineyards, or other crops.

questions.question: Are small enclosed vegetated plots grouped together?
questions.definition: Count at least five adjacent bounded plots each under approximately 100 meters across, with visible vegetation in most plots.

questions.question: Does a broad open area contain curved parallel bands?
questions.definition: Count at least three resolved bands that curve together within one field-like or managed-looking surface.

questions.question: Are apparent management boundaries clearer in false color than in true color?
questions.definition: Count at least two field or plot boundaries that strongly separate vegetation signals in false color while remaining subdued in true color.

questions.question: Does an abrupt change in parcel size divide the agricultural-looking part of the patch?
questions.definition: Count adjoining groups of at least three parcels where typical visible parcel area differs by approximately a factor of four.

questions.question: Are built-looking surfaces interspersed with substantial vegetation?
questions.definition: Count at least three resolved roof or paved clusters separated by vegetation areas of comparable or greater width.

questions.question: Is a built-looking area concentrated in one compact cluster?
questions.definition: Count a cluster covering at least 5% of the patch and containing more than three-quarters of its identifiable roof and paved surfaces.

questions.question: Are built-looking clusters scattered across the patch?
questions.definition: Count at least three distinct clusters separated from one another by approximately 100 meters or more of open or vegetated ground.

questions.question: Do built-looking features form a ribbon along a visible route?
questions.definition: Count roof-like clusters distributed along at least 300 meters of one road-like corridor with a developed strip much longer than it is wide.

questions.question: Is there a sharp boundary between a built-looking area and open ground?
questions.definition: Count a boundary at least 200 meters long where a roof-and-paving pattern ends abruptly against vegetation or exposed soil.

questions.question: Does the density of built-looking surfaces decrease gradually toward open ground?
questions.definition: Count a transition at least approximately 150 meters wide in which roof-like clusters become progressively more separated by vegetation or bare ground.

questions.question: Does a road-like corridor cross a predominantly open part of the patch?
questions.definition: Count a continuous linear route at least 400 meters long with vegetated or bare ground along most of both sides.

questions.question: Do visible road-like routes form at least two junctions?
questions.definition: Count clear connections among continuous route-like lines, excluding apparent crossings whose connection cannot be resolved.

questions.question: Does a road-like route visibly curve around a large surface feature?
questions.definition: Count a route bending along the edge of a distinct area for at least approximately 150 meters.

questions.question: Does a straight transport-like corridor cut across otherwise irregular boundaries?
questions.definition: Count an approximately straight route at least 400 meters long that crosses or truncates at least three irregular surface boundaries.

questions.question: Are pale hard-looking surfaces grouped with angular roof-like features?
questions.definition: Count a connected built-looking complex approximately 100 meters across containing both resolved angular roofs and adjoining relatively smooth pale ground.

questions.question: Are both compact and loosely spaced built patterns visible?
questions.definition: Count one area with mostly contiguous roof-and-paving texture and another where comparable built clusters are separated by substantial vegetation.

questions.question: Do built-looking surfaces occupy between 5% and 30% of the patch?
questions.definition: Estimate the combined extent of identifiable roofs, paved yards, and broad roads while excluding uncertain bare-soil surfaces.

questions.question: Does a substantial vegetated opening lie within a built-looking area?
questions.definition: Count a vegetated area approximately 100 meters across bordered on at least three sides by roof-and-paving patterns.

questions.question: Do vegetation strips follow visible roads?
questions.definition: Count vegetation aligned along at least 300 meters of a road-like route rather than merely crossing it.

questions.question: Does a road-like feature separate two contrasting vegetation patterns?
questions.definition: Count a visible route with consistently different vegetation color, texture, or parcel arrangement on its two sides for at least 200 meters.

questions.question: Are angular bare or hard-looking clearings visible beside built features?
questions.definition: Count at least two resolved nonvegetated clearings with geometric edges adjoining identifiable roof-like surfaces.

questions.question: Does a connected network of pale lines divide vegetation into blocks?
questions.definition: Count road- or track-like lines forming boundaries around at least three vegetated blocks, without requiring a specific route classification.

questions.question: Are visibly larger roof-like structures mixed with smaller built clusters?
questions.definition: Count at least one resolved angular roof footprint approximately four times the area of nearby distinguishable roof-like features.

questions.question: Do built-looking features occupy a junction between several surface types?
questions.definition: Count a roof-and-paving cluster directly adjoining at least three visibly distinct surroundings such as fields, woody vegetation, open soil, or water.

questions.question: Does an open nonvegetated area have both geometric edges and internal irregularity?
questions.definition: Count an area covering at least 2% of the patch with straight outer boundaries but visibly mottled, disturbed-looking, or uneven interior texture.

questions.question: Are human-shaped features concentrated around the edges of a larger vegetated area?
questions.definition: Count roads, angular clearings, or built clusters along at least half the visible perimeter of a vegetation block covering 10% or more of the patch.

questions.question: Does a narrow route penetrate a large woody-looking block?
questions.definition: Count a continuous road- or track-like opening extending at least approximately 200 meters into coarse-textured vegetation.

questions.question: Does the patch contain a visible transition from a field pattern to a street-and-building pattern?
questions.definition: Count adjoining areas with clearly recognizable agricultural parcel geometry on one side and connected routes with roof-like clusters on the other.

questions.question: Are built-looking features aligned with the surrounding parcel boundaries?
questions.definition: Count at least three resolved built features or clusters whose principal orientation broadly matches neighboring field or plot edges.

questions.question: Does apparent open water share a substantial boundary with vegetation?
questions.definition: Count a smooth water-like surface with a weak near-infrared response adjoining vegetation along at least approximately 100 meters, excluding obvious shadows.

questions.question: Does a water-like feature have an elongated shape?
questions.definition: Count a coherent apparent water surface at least three times longer than wide and at least approximately 100 meters long.

questions.question: Is a water-like surface bordered by a distinct vegetation strip?
questions.definition: Count a resolved vegetation band following at least 100 meters of an apparent shoreline and differing from the land farther away.

questions.question: Does apparent water occur within a mosaic of fields or built surfaces?
questions.definition: Count a resolved water-like feature with field-like parcels or built-looking surfaces along at least half its visible land-facing boundary.

questions.question: Does a dark, sinuous corridor pass through open ground?
questions.definition: Count a winding corridor at least 200 meters long that is darker than adjacent open surfaces in both images and is not an obvious cast shadow.

questions.question: Are dark smooth patches embedded in a vegetated area?
questions.definition: Count at least two coherent dark patches approximately 30 meters across with weak vegetation signals and no clear association with shadow-casting objects.

questions.question: Does exposed ground contain a broad dark area consistent with wetter-looking soil?
questions.definition: Count a smooth dark zone at least approximately 50 meters across within otherwise lighter soil-like ground, treating darkness as an appearance rather than proof of moisture.

questions.question: Do dark soil-like patches follow a branching pattern?
questions.definition: Count connected dark areas within exposed ground with at least two branch points, excluding vegetation strips and recognizable shadows.

questions.question: Is stronger vegetation associated with a dark or water-like corridor?
questions.definition: Count a vegetation band with a stronger red response than nearby vegetation that follows at least 100 meters of a dark smooth corridor.

questions.question: Do dark and pale soil-like areas alternate within one open surface?
questions.definition: Count at least two dark and two pale resolved zones within a connected bare-looking area, excluding obvious vegetation and shadow.

questions.question: Does a broad darkening pattern cross a visible parcel boundary?
questions.definition: Count a coherent dark zone continuing across at least two neighboring open parcels without being explained by a common shadow.

questions.question: Are dark ground patches concentrated along the margins of open areas?
questions.definition: Count at least two nonshadow dark patches located along field or clearing edges with lighter ground toward the corresponding interiors.

questions.question: Does a dark surface grade gradually into lighter exposed ground?
questions.definition: Count a continuous tonal transition approximately 50 meters wide or more between dark and light soil-like surfaces without a sharp vegetation boundary.

questions.question: Are narrow dark lines accompanied by vegetation on both sides?
questions.definition: Count at least 150 meters of resolved dark linear surface flanked by vegetation, excluding obvious shadows cast along a single woody edge.

questions.question: Do visibly wet-looking or water-like surfaces form an irregular boundary with dry-looking open ground?
questions.definition: Count smooth dark or water-like ground adjoining lighter exposed ground along a boundary with at least two clear bends, without asserting actual moisture content.

questions.question: Are the strongest vegetation signals concentrated in narrow features rather than broad blocks?
questions.definition: Count this pattern when more than half the conspicuously strongest red vegetation occupies strips under approximately 50 meters wide.

questions.question: Do woody-looking vegetation and field-like parcels contribute comparable areas?
questions.definition: Count both patterns when each covers at least 20% of the patch and neither occupies more than twice the area of the other.

questions.question: Does a built-looking cluster adjoin both woody vegetation and open fields?
questions.definition: Count a single resolved roof-and-paving cluster sharing visible boundaries with coarse-textured vegetation and field-like open ground.

questions.question: Does a linear vegetation feature connect a built-looking area to a larger vegetation block?
questions.definition: Count a continuous visible vegetation strip linking the edge of a roof-and-paving cluster to a vegetation block approximately 100 meters across or larger.

questions.question: Are the smallest parcels concentrated near built-looking features?
questions.definition: Count a group of at least three parcels next to a built cluster whose typical visible area is less than half that of parcels farther away.

questions.question: Does a road-like route follow the boundary between woody vegetation and open ground?
questions.definition: Count a visible route running along that boundary for at least approximately 200 meters.

questions.question: Do open areas form fingers extending into woody-looking vegetation?
questions.definition: Count at least two open projections approximately 100 meters long bordered on both sides by coarse-textured vegetation.

questions.question: Do woody vegetation strips divide open land into enclosed compartments?
questions.definition: Count at least three open compartments each bounded on three or more sides by resolved coarse-textured vegetation strips.

questions.question: Are strong and weak vegetation signals associated with different parcel sizes?
questions.definition: Count at least two predominantly strong-signal parcels and two predominantly weak-signal parcels whose typical visible areas differ by approximately a factor of two.

questions.question: Is the vegetation around built-looking features less continuous than vegetation farther away?
questions.definition: Compare a belt approximately 100 meters around a built cluster with a similarly sized vegetated area elsewhere, requiring clearly more nonvegetated interruptions near the cluster.

questions.question: Does a continuous pale corridor interrupt an otherwise connected vegetation pattern?
questions.definition: Count a road-like or bare-ground band extending at least 300 meters with substantial vegetation on both sides and no resolved vegetation connection across it.

questions.question: Are irregular vegetation boundaries juxtaposed with regular field boundaries?
questions.definition: Count a woody-looking or rough vegetation area with a curved edge directly adjoining at least three straight-sided field-like parcels.

questions.question: Do vegetation strips remain visually strong beside weakly vegetated fields?
questions.definition: Count at least two field margins with conspicuous red vegetation signals beside parcel interiors that are mostly pale, brown, or weakly red.

questions.question: Does a bare-looking opening interrupt a strong vegetation signal?
questions.definition: Count an opening approximately 50 meters across or larger with little vegetation response embedded in or cutting into a predominantly strong-red area.

questions.question: Do neighboring smooth and woody-looking vegetation areas show opposite brightness rankings in the two images?
questions.definition: Count an adjoining pair where the area appearing lighter in true color appears darker in false color, using broad interiors rather than edge pixels.

questions.question: Are straight and winding linear features both prominent?
questions.definition: Count at least one approximately straight feature and one feature with multiple clear bends, each extending at least 300 meters.

questions.question: Does one corridor cross several contrasting land-use patterns?
questions.definition: Count a continuous road-like, water-like, or vegetated corridor passing through at least three visibly distinct patterns such as fields, woody blocks, or built clusters.

questions.question: Are nonvegetated surfaces more connected than the vegetation between them?
questions.definition: Count a connected nonvegetated network spanning the patch while the substantial vegetated areas within it remain visibly separated.

questions.question: Are small nonvegetated areas embedded in a connected vegetation matrix?
questions.definition: Count at least five resolved nonvegetated areas separated from one another by vegetation that remains visibly connected around them.

questions.question: Does surface heterogeneity increase near a major boundary?
questions.definition: Count a belt approximately 100 meters wide around a major boundary containing at least three surface appearances while the adjoining broad interiors are relatively uniform.

questions.question: Do similarly colored true-color areas separate into different patterns in false color?
questions.definition: Count at least two substantial areas with similar true-color appearance but clearly different false-color vegetation responses or textures.

questions.question: Do differently colored true-color areas share a similar strong vegetation response?
questions.definition: Count at least two areas approximately 100 meters across with clearly different true-color hues but comparably strong red vegetation signals.

questions.question: Does a dark linear feature coincide with a change in parcel orientation?
questions.definition: Count a nonshadow dark corridor with at least three parcel boundaries on each side whose dominant orientations differ visibly.

questions.question: Are dark ground patches spatially associated with stronger vegetation?
questions.definition: Count at least two nonshadow dark soil-like or water-like patches directly adjoining vegetation that is redder in false color than vegetation farther away.

questions.question: Does the patch contain both a connected woody block and isolated woody-looking remnants?
questions.definition: Count one coarse-textured vegetation block covering at least 10% of the patch plus at least three separated smaller clumps with similar texture.

questions.question: Do broad open areas contrast with a dense network of narrow vegetated boundaries?
questions.definition: Count at least three open areas approximately 100 meters across separated by connected vegetation strips under approximately 50 meters wide.

questions.question: Do two contrasting surface types recur on both sides of a major route?
questions.definition: Count a road-like corridor at least 300 meters long with substantial examples of the same two distinct surface types visible on each side.

questions.question: Is a small-scale mosaic enclosed on several sides by larger uniform areas?
questions.definition: Count a cluster of at least five small surface units bordered on three sides by areas each approximately 200 meters across or larger.

questions.question: Does the strongest vegetation contrast occur within managed-looking land rather than along its outer edge?
questions.definition: Count a field or plot complex whose clearest false-color vegetation difference separates internal parcels and exceeds the contrast along most of its external boundary.

questions.question: Does a narrow feature coincide with changes in both surface color and spatial organization?
questions.definition: Count a road-like, water-like, or vegetated line at least 200 meters long separating sides that differ in dominant color and in parcel size, texture, or built density.
